instructions:
DogLog Studio shows FRC robot logs (WPILOG files) and live robot data on dashboards. With these commands you can build and arrange dashboards for the user, save images of them to check how they look, save videos of them to share, open a log or connect to the robot, move the timeline cursor to a moment, and change settings.

Each dashboard's layout is a tree: a split puts its children side by side (`row`) or stacks them (`column`), and each leaf is a pane. A pane shows one widget, or nothing. A widget's bindings are the entries it shows, bound by entry name. `dashboard_get` returns the IDs other commands take, and points out bindings that won't show what you meant.

Commands never return entry values. To analyze data, ex. to find when something happened, read the log with the wpilog-parser library (and its skill, if you have it), then show the user that moment with `timeline_update`.

commands.name: window_list
commands.description: List open Studio windows: each one's ID, when it was last focused, the dashboard it shows, its source, and whether it's focused. Use a window's ID as the `window` input of other commands to target it, otherwise they act on the most recently focused window.

commands.name: window_update
commands.description: Show a dashboard in the window, bring the window to the front, or both.

focus.description: Whether to bring the window to the front

commands.name: dashboard_list
commands.description: List dashboards in sidebar order, with whether each is shared with everyone connected to the robot, and which one is shown.

commands.name: dashboard_get
commands.description: Get a dashboard: its name, layout, and each pane's widget, options, and bindings, with the IDs other commands take. `problems` point out what keeps a widget from showing what was meant, ex. an entry missing from the source, an entry type the widget doesn't accept, or a role that doesn't fit. Sizes are each pane or split's share of its parent split.

commands.name: dashboard_capture
commands.description: Save a PNG image of a dashboard, or one of its panes, as the user would copy it: with the window's theme, sizes, and timeline cursor, and the timeline below a whole dashboard. Shows the dashboard, restoring the window if it's minimized, and waits for its widgets to load first. Returns the image's path, open it to check that widgets look as meant.

paneId.description: Only this pane. Left out, the whole dashboard.

path.description: Absolute path to save the PNG to. Left out, it goes in a new file in the temporary folder.

commands.name: dashboard_record
commands.description: Save an MP4 video of a dashboard from `start` to `end`, the same video Export video saves: 30 frames a second at the source's original timing, with the window's theme and sizes, and the timeline below. Shows the dashboard in video export mode while it saves, where the user sees its progress and can cancel, then returns the window to how it was. Saving can take about as long as the video. Returns the video's path.

start.description: Seconds on the source's clock, see `timeline_get`. Times outside the source's range go to its start or end.

end.description: Seconds on the source's clock, see `timeline_get`. Times outside the source's range go to its start or end. After `start`.

path.description: Absolute path to save the MP4 to. Left out, it goes in a new file in the temporary folder.

commands.name: dashboard_create
commands.description: Create a dashboard at the top of the list and show it, optionally with a whole layout of panes, widgets, and bindings. An invalid layout creates nothing. At most 4 panes fit side by side, or stacked. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

name.description: Left out, a name is suggested from the dashboard's contents

layout.description: Left out, the dashboard has one empty pane

widget.description: Left out, the pane is empty

bindings.description: Entries to show, in order. Accepted kinds: number, boolean, string. Left out, the widget starts like one the user adds.

entry.description: Full entry name, ex. `/Robot/Drive/Pose`. Entries missing from the source can be bound too.

color.description: One of the theme's 5 chart colors, by index. Left out, the widget picks one.

hidden.description: Listed in the legend but not drawn

role.description: How the widget shows the entry. Left out, it's inferred from the entry and the bindings before it.

oneOf.description: Graph: Plots entries over time. Numbers go on the left or right axis (`left`, `right`), or are shown as colored bands (`discrete`); booleans and strings can only be bands. A number goes on the right axis when its unit measures something else than the left axis's.

view.description: View, `2d` by default. `null` goes back to inferring it or the default.

coordinates.description: WPILib coordinates, `blue-wall` by default. `null` goes back to inferring it or the default.

orientation.description: Orientation, `blue-left` by default. `null` goes back to inferring it or the default.

stagedGamePieces.description: Staged game pieces, `shown` by default. `null` goes back to inferring it or the default.

bindings.description: Entries to show, in order. Accepted kinds: struct, struct[], mechanism2d. Left out, the widget starts like one the user adds.

entry.description: Full entry name, ex. `/Robot/Drive/Pose`. Entries missing from the source can be bound too.

color.description: One of the theme's 5 chart colors, by index. Left out, the widget picks one.

hidden.description: Listed in the legend but not drawn

role.description: How the widget shows the entry. Left out, it's inferred from the entry and the bindings before it.

robot.description: A robot or ghost's robot in 3D: `swerve` (a simple swerve robot) or the name of a robot project the user added on their device. Left out, it's the first robot's.

connectedFrom.description: Indexes of this widget's bindings (from 0) to draw lines from, ex. from the robot to seen AprilTags. Each must be a single robot, ghost, or point.

oneOf.description: Field: The FRC field, seen from above or in 3D (the `view` option, `2d` or `3d`). Pose2d and Pose3d can be a `robot`, `ghost` (ex. a setpoint), or `point`; the first pose is the robot and later ones ghosts. Translations are a `point`. Pose and translation arrays are `points` or a `path` (inferred from names like `path` or `trajectory`). Rectangle2d and Ellipse2d (and arrays of them) are a `shape`. A single robot, ghost, or point can be connected to another binding to draw lines from it, ex. from the robot to the AprilTags it sees. In 3D, a Pose3d[] can place a robot project's `parts` (inferred from names containing `component`), and Mechanism2d entries are drawn on a robot's `side` (XZ, the default), `front` (YZ), or `top` (XY) plane; connect them from a robot or ghost to attach them to it, or they're drawn on the only robot. Each robot and ghost binding can pick its `robot`, as in the robot widget's option, defaulting to the first robot's. The `view` option is inferred as 3D when a parts or mechanism binding is bound. The `coordinates` option is `blue-wall` (WPILib 2026, origin at the blue alliance wall) or `center` (WPILib 2027, origin at the center with +X toward blue), inferred from the WPILib version the robot published. The `orientation` option supports landscape (`blue-left`, `red-left`) and portrait (`blue-top`, `red-top`), and defaults to putting +X on the right, in 3D the camera starts turned the same way. The `stagedGamePieces` option (`shown` or `hidden`) draws the game pieces staged at the start of a match in 3D.

direction.description: `row` puts panes side by side, left to right. `column` stacks them, top to bottom.

children.description: Panes or splits, left to right or top to bottom

commands.name: dashboard_update
commands.description: Rename a dashboard, or share it or stop sharing it with everyone connected to the robot. Stopping sharing deletes it for everyone else and gives it a new ID. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

name.description: A blank name goes back to suggesting one from its contents

commands.name: dashboard_delete
commands.description: Close a dashboard, like the user closing it. The user can reopen it. Closing a shared dashboard deletes it for everyone.

commands.name: dashboard_duplicate
commands.description: Copy a dashboard, the copy goes right below it and is shown. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

commands.name: dashboard_combine
commands.description: Put dashboards' panes side by side in the first of them, in order, close the others, and show it. Fails when more than 4 panes would be side by side. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

commands.name: pane_create
commands.description: Split a pane to add one after it (to its right, or below it), optionally showing a widget. At most 4 panes fit side by side, or stacked. Returns the new pane's ID and the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

direction.description: `row` adds the pane to the right, `column` below. Left out, it splits along the pane's longer side, as when the user adds a widget.

widget.description: Left out, the new pane is empty

commands.name: pane_move
commands.description: Move a pane beside another pane of the same dashboard. The panes around its old place take its space. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

targetPaneId.description: The pane to put it beside, from `dashboard_get`

side.description: Which side of the target pane it goes on

commands.name: pane_delete
commands.description: Remove a pane, the panes beside it take its space. Removing the only pane leaves an empty pane. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

commands.name: binding_create
commands.description: Bind entries to a pane's widget by name, after its other bindings. An entry can be bound more than once, ex. to show it two ways. Returns the new bindings' IDs and the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

entry.description: Full entry name, ex. `/Robot/Drive/Pose`. Entries missing from the source can be bound too.

role.description: How the widget shows the entry, one of the widget type's roles (see `dashboard_create`). Left out, it's inferred as when the user drops the entry on the widget.

color.description: One of the theme's 5 chart colors, by index. Left out, the widget picks one.

hidden.description: Listed in the legend but not drawn

commands.name: binding_update
commands.description: Change a binding's role, color, hidden state, robot, or connections. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

role.description: One of the widget type's roles that fits the entry

color.description: One of the theme's 5 chart colors, by index. Left out, the widget picks one. `null` lets the widget pick again.

anyOf.description: One of the theme's 5 chart colors, by index. Left out, the widget picks one.

hidden.description: Listed in the legend but not drawn

robot.description: A robot or ghost's robot in 3D: `swerve` (a simple swerve robot) or the name of a robot project the user added on their device. `null` uses the first robot's again.

anyOf.description: A robot or ghost's robot in 3D: `swerve` (a simple swerve robot) or the name of a robot project the user added on their device

connectedFrom.description: IDs of the bindings in the same field widget to draw lines from, replacing the current ones. Each must be a single robot, ghost, or point.

commands.name: binding_delete
commands.description: Unbind an entry from its widget. Returns the dashboard like `dashboard_get`.

commands.name: entry_list
commands.description: List the active source's entries, with each one's name, type, kind, and metadata (ex. its unit). Never returns values.

name.description: Only entries whose name contains this, ignoring case

kind.description: Only entries of this kind. `unsupported` entries can't be shown by widgets.

commands.name: source_get
commands.description: Get the active source: a log file, or a live connection to the robot or simulator, with its status and how many entries it has. `null` when there's none.

commands.name: source_update
commands.description: Open a WPILOG file, or connect to the robot from the `robotTarget` setting (or the simulator when the robot isn't reachable). Returns once the log is loaded or the connection is made, like `source_get`.

path.description: Absolute path of a WPILOG file to open. Left out, connects to the robot instead.

commands.name: source_delete
commands.description: Close the active source, leaving none.

commands.name: source_export
commands.description: Save everything the live session received as a WPILOG file, to read with wpilog-parser, whether or not the live session is shown. Its times are on the robot's clock, so they line up with the robot's own logs but not `timeline_get`. Returns the file's path.

path.description: Absolute path to save the file to. Left out, it goes in a new file in the temporary folder.

commands.name: timeline_get
commands.description: Get the timeline cursor and the source's time range, in seconds on the source's clock: a log's timestamps (microseconds, as wpilog-parser reads them) divided by 1,000,000. Studio shows times relative to `start`.

commands.name: timeline_update
commands.description: Move the timeline cursor so the user's dashboards show that moment. Stops following live data. Returns the timeline like `timeline_get`.

time.description: Seconds on the source's clock, see `timeline_get`. Times outside the source's range go to its start or end.

commands.name: settings_get
commands.description: Get the settings from Studio's Settings page.

commands.name: settings_update
commands.description: Change settings from Studio's Settings page. Returns every setting like `settings_get`.

themePreset.description: Theme color: Team 581 maroon (`team581`), match13 blue, `neutral` gray, or `custom` for `themeColor`

themeColor.description: Hex color the `custom` theme preset is generated from, ex. `#1c1816`

reduceMotion.description: Whether to skip animations even when the system doesn't ask to reduce motion

name.description: The user's name, shown to others in shared dashboards. Blank shows an anonymous name.

robotTarget.description: Team number or IP address of the robot, ex. `581` or `10.5.81.2`. Connecting uses it.

mediaControls.description: Whether media keys and the system media controls play, pause, and seek logs

naturalScrolling.description: Whether scrolling the timeline follows natural scrolling, in browsers that don't report it
